definitions.explanation: Sesame seeds with a pale cream to white hull. The most commonly used variety of sesame in Japanese cooking, with a mild, delicate flavor.

examples.japanese: {白|しろ}ごまを{振|ふ}りかける。
{白|しろ}ごまは{料理|りょうり}の{仕上|しあ}げによく{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: White sesame is often used as a finishing touch in cooking.

examples.japanese: {白|しろ}ごまを{擂|す}ってドレッシングに{混|ま}ぜると、まろやかな{風味|ふうみ}になる。
examples.english: If you grind white sesame and mix it into the dressing, it gives a mellow flavor.

notes:
A compound of {白|しろ} (white) and ごま ({胡麻|ごま}, sesame). White sesame is the most commonly used sesame variety in Japan, accounting for the majority of sesame consumption. It has a milder flavor than {黒|くろ}ごま (black sesame).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {白|しろ}ごまを{擂|す}る: to grind white sesame
- {白|しろ}{炒|い}りごま: toasted white sesame
- {白|しろ}{擂|す}りごま: ground white sesame
- {白|しろ}{練|ね}りごま: white sesame paste

RELATED WORDS:
- {黒|くろ}ごま: black sesame seeds — stronger, nuttier flavor; popular in sweets
- {金|きん}ごま: golden sesame seeds — a rarer variety with a rich aroma
- {胡麻|ごま}: sesame — the general term
- {炒|い}りごま: toasted sesame — the most common prepared form
- すりごま: ground sesame

USAGE:
White sesame appears everywhere in Japanese cooking: as a garnish on rice, in {胡麻|ごま}{和|あ}え (sesame-dressed vegetables), in dressings and sauces, and in {白|しろ}ごまプリン (white sesame pudding). On packaging, look for {白|しろ}いりごま (toasted) or {白|しろ}すりごま (ground).
